architecture: Keep Classic ASP page flow separate from shared include/helper responsibilities.
Validate all request input on the server and encode untrusted output for the correct context.
Use parameterized ADO commands and least-privilege identities for database workflows.
Separate protected configuration/data/logs from public site files.
Document COM/ADO dependencies and test the exact IIS environment.
milestone_notes: Requirements and data model: State the use cases, data fields, request routes, and authorization rules.; Identify runtime/provider assumptions and sensitive-data boundaries.
Build the minimal vertical slice: Implement one complete happy path using synthetic data.; Keep shared includes, configuration, persistence, and presentation responsibilities clear.

Validation, security, and failure cases: Test a normal case, an invalid/boundary case, and a dependency failure.; Apply server-side authorization, safe output encoding, and parameterized SQL where relevant.
Verification and handoff: Provide a test matrix, observed results, version/dependency notes, and reset/rollback steps.; List untested items without claiming deployment or production verification.
expected_artifacts: Working local test-site implementation or a clearly labelled design/test harness where execution dependencies are unavailable.
Synthetic fixtures, expected output, negative/boundary cases, environment notes, and recovery guidance.
answer.review_warning: Reference outline only; it is not a claim that the full project or a live IIS deployment was executed.
